description:
Code, verification checks and outputs for the revised manuscript "Error robustness of doublet and triplet genetic codes" (Ribbeck, Paudyal and Kiran; revision of a submission to the Journal of Molecular Evolution).

This version withdraws the conclusion of v1.0.0. The z-scores in v1.0.0 came from a null model that permuted amino-acid labels among individual codons, not among synonymous blocks as described. With every amino acid made equidistant from every other, that null reproduces the v1.0.0 values (z = -17.07 for the standard code), so those z-scores measured how tightly synonymous codons cluster, not error minimization, and the doublet-triplet contrast they supported does not hold. The v1.0.0 files are unchanged in this archive for the record.

Revised results. The minimum expected cost of a single-nucleotide misreading per translated residue, at fixed amino-acid usage, does not depend on codon length: without physicochemical distances this follows from the edge-isoperimetric inequality for Hamming graphs, and with distances certified searches give identical doublet and triplet optima under uniform usage and a 1.6% difference under proteome usage. A longer code gains only by making its noisiest position synonymous; at in vitro misreading rates that position is the third, which the standard code silences. A quadruplet code gains 2 to 6% over the best triplet code found. Under the block-preserving null the standard code's assignment is significant but modest (p = 0.0005 to 0.027 across descriptor representations).

Contents added in v2.0.0. revision/: manuscript, response to the reviewer, figures and supplementary material (PDF). reviewer_response/: rebuilt AAindex descriptor matrix and its rules (descriptor_rebuild/), certified optima (arch_cert/, usage_cert/, rebuild_opt10/, rebuild_opt20/, n4/, finish/), position-specific misreading rates and models (position_rates/, position_model/, position_empirical/, rebuild_grid/, rebuild_grid2/), and closing checks (rebuild_close/). paper_reanalysis/: the reanalysis that identified the null-model error. Third-party supplementary data are not redistributed; reviewer_response/position_rates/raw/README.md gives sources and checksums. An exploratory analysis of proteome substitution data that is not part of the revised manuscript is withheld; the code module it shares with descriptor_rebuild/stats.py is included.
